title: F265: a documented flag's VALUES are checked against the parser that takes them
description: P25's review found a defect the whole gate set was blind to: commands/status.md advertised --view active|pending|archived|all while the parser took three, so a value copied out of the documentation exited 2. _refs.command_flag_drift compares flag NAMES between two documents and never asks a parser anything, so nothing in the tree could see it. Measured: 10 argparse flags in the plugin constrain their values and 5 command docs advertise a value list; the other four were correct, so this is a missing instrument rather than a backlog. A static AST reader resolves only 1 of the 5 - the rest spell choices=list(_cli_fmt.MODES) or sorted(_vocab.VIEW_SEGS) - so the check must construct the parser and read argparse's own answer.
desiredOutcome: Every value list a command doc advertises is exactly the set its parser accepts, in both directions, and a script that hides its parser is a finding rather than a silent skip.

findings: The first version reported a census hole whenever a command doc named a script with no readable parser, which convicted `doctor.md` for printing a `run-test-gate.py` invocation in its prose. Narrowed to context on a real finding; the wrong test case that had frozen it (ch6) was corrected too.

summary: F265, found by shipping it inside P25: `commands/status.md` advertised `--view active|pending|archived|all` while the parser took three, and the whole gate set was green because nothing compares a documented flag's VALUES to what its parser accepts. `_help.command_choice_drift()` constructs each command's parser and asks argparse itself, in both directions - it cannot read the source, because four of the five value lists in the plugin are calls rather than literals. It earned its keep on the first run: F266, four `/audit:usage --by` values that worked and were documented nowhere. The first version over-fired and convicted `doctor.md` for printing another tool's command in its prose; the live case caught it.

tasks.title: audit-doctor.py exposes build_parser(), so its options are reachable without running it
tasks.description: audit-status.py and audit-usage.py already build their parser in a module-level build_parser(); audit-doctor.py builds it inside main(), where nothing but a process can reach it. Extract it to match, which is a refactor with no behaviour change - main() calls build_parser().parse_args(argv) - and is what lets a lint ask argparse for a flag's choices instead of guessing them from the AST.

add: test_audit_doctor.py: build_parser() is reachable and its --color choices are _cli_fmt.MODES, and main() still parses the same arguments

tasks.title: _help.command_choice_drift(): the advertised values are the parser's, both directions
tasks.description: For every command doc carrying an argument-hint, find the value lists it advertises (--flag a|b|c), resolve the doc to the scripts it names, construct each script's parser and read the flag's choices off argparse itself. A value advertised and not accepted is the defect that shipped; a value accepted and not advertised is the same fault facing the other way and is reported too. A doc that names a script with no build_parser() is a FINDING rather than a skip, or a script could opt out of the check by hiding its parser. IT LIVES IN _help AND NOT _refs, and that is a layer fact: constructing a parser needs _loader, and _refs is layer 1 beside it, so it cannot import it - which is exactly why schema_vocab_drift sits in _help too, a layer up from the vocabulary it grades. Cases in test__help.py and rows in both prove-gates tables, since a lint with a row in neither is invisible to the coverage rule itself.

add: test__help.py: a doc advertising a value the parser refuses is a finding, and so is a value the parser takes that the doc omits
test__help.py: a command doc whose script exposes no parser is reported rather than skipped
